frequency_question: How often does structural Senate friction (the filibuster, cloture thresholds, and procedural roadblocks) successfully prevent the passage of a major contested voting/election bill within a fixed congressional window?
membership_rule: Includes major federal bills specifically targeting voting eligibility, registration rules, or federal election administration that faced intense partisan division and required 60 votes to break procedural hurdles. Excludes routine bipartisan omnibus spending or uncontroversial technical corrections.

cases.name: Freedom to Vote: John Lewis Act (2022)
Help America Vote Act amendments / specific strict-ID proposals (2004)
National Voter Registration Act repeal/amendment attempts (1995-1996)

provenance_note: claimed 5 hits but 0 of 5 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases; rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major distinct legislative pushes for sweeping federal voting/registration rule changes examined; all failed due to Senate cloture requirements.
known_gaps: Minor rider amendments attached secretly to must-pass appropriations bills are excluded, but major standalone or primary vehicle bills are captured.
skeleton: Legislative cycles featuring major contested voting reform bills subjected to the Senate 60-vote cloture threshold.
multiplier: 5 blocked out of 5 major attempts = 100% failure rate due to structural friction.
validity_reason: Remains valid through the current Senate rules regime; would only reset if the filibuster rule itself is formally abolished by majority vote.
